source_text: Voluntas itaque motus est animi, in iure suo habentis utrum sinisterior ad prava decurrat, an dexterior ad celsa contendat.
pass_a_gloss: Will therefore is a movement of the mind, having in its own right whether it run more leftward toward crooked things, or more rightward strive toward high things.

lemmas.lexica: LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: Will, then, is a movement of the mind that has under its own control whether it runs to the left toward wrongdoing or strives to the right toward higher things.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
